subject: tech
title: Steps in Order
about: An algorithm is a list of steps in order, like brushing teeth or making a sandwich, and a computer follows its steps exactly, so the order matters (K2-AP-01, K2-AP-04). The cards ask what comes first, next and last, and how to break a big job into small steps. Read it together: the word algorithm is new, but the idea is one he already lives every morning.
tip: Say the steps of something you are doing right now, like making lunch, and ask him what would go wrong if two of them swapped places.

cards.q: A list of steps you follow in order has a special name. What is it?
cards.note: Algorithm is a big word for a list of steps in order. Say it: AL-go-rith-um.

cards.q: A cookie recipe lists the steps in order. So a recipe is a kind of what?
cards.note: A recipe is an algorithm for food: step one, step two, step three, cookies!

cards.q: You brush your teeth. What comes first?
cards.note: First the toothpaste goes on. Then you brush. Then you spit and rinse.

cards.q: You brush your teeth. What comes last?
cards.note: Last means the very end. The brush goes back in its cup when everything else is done.

cards.q: You make a jelly sandwich. What is the first step?
cards.note: You cannot spread jelly on bread you have not taken out yet. First things first.

cards.q: You spread jelly on the bread. What comes next?
cards.note: Next means the step right after this one.

cards.q: You are getting dressed. What do you put on right before your shoes?
cards.note: Socks first, then shoes. If a robot did shoes first, the socks would not fit!

cards.q: A robot's steps say: put on shoes, then put on socks. What happens?
cards.note: A computer does exactly what the steps say, even when it looks silly. The order matters.

cards.q: Your steps say spread the jelly, but you forgot to say open the jar. What does a computer do?
cards.note: A computer only does what the steps say. People fill in missing steps; computers cannot.

cards.q: You plant a seed. What is the first step?
cards.note: Hole, seed, cover, water, wait, flower. Each step gets the next one ready.

cards.q: You plant a seed. Which step comes last?
cards.note: Some steps are fast and some, like waiting, take days and days.

cards.q: You close the toy box lid, then try to put the toy in. What is wrong?
cards.note: Toy in first, then lid. When steps come out of order, the job goes wrong.

cards.q: Cleaning your room is a big job. What makes a big job easier?
cards.note: Big job, small steps: books on the shelf, toys in the box, clothes in the basket. One at a time.

cards.q: Which is a small step of cleaning your room?
cards.note: A small step is one thing you can finish. Then you start the next one.

cards.q: Wake up, eat breakfast, go to school. Which comes next after wake up?
cards.note: Next is the step right after. Last is the very end.

cards.q: Wake up, eat breakfast, go to school. Which step is last?
cards.note: First, next, last. School is the end of this list.

cards.q: You wash your hands. What comes first?
cards.note: Water on, wet hands, soap, scrub, rinse, water off, dry. Seven little steps!

cards.q: You tell a robot: walk 3 steps, then turn. What does the robot do?
cards.note: Robots and computers do exactly what the steps say, no more and no less.
